sn44.3:1.1: On one occasion the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahakoṭṭhita were dwelling at Baraṇasī in the Deer Park at Isipatana.
sn44.3:1.2: Then, in the evening, the Venerable Mahakoṭṭhita emerged from seclusion and approached the Venerable Sāriputta. He exchanged greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta and,
sn44.3:1.3: when they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to him:
sn44.3:2.1: “How is it, friend Sāriputta, does the Tathagata exist after death?”
sn44.3:2.2: “Friend, the Blessed One has not declared this:
sn44.3:2.6: As in the preceding sutta down to:
sn44.3:2.7: “Friend, the Blessed One has not declared this either:
sn44.3:2.10: ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”
sn44.3:3.1: When asked, ‘How is it, friend, does the Tathagata exist after death?’ … And when asked, ‘Then, friend, does the Tathagata neither exist nor not exist after death?’—in each case you say: ‘Friend, the Blessed One has not declared this.’
sn44.3:3.6: What now, friend, is the cause and reason why this has not been declared by the Blessed One?”
sn44.3:4.1: “‘The Tathagata exists after death’: this, friend, is an involvement with form.
sn44.3:4.2: ‘The Tathagata does not exist after death’: this is an involvement with form.
sn44.3:4.3: ‘The Tathagata both exists and does not exist after death’: this is an involvement with form.
sn44.3:4.4: ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death’: this is an involvement with form.
sn44.3:4.5: “‘The Tathagata exists after death’: this, friend, is an involvement with feeling …
sn44.3:4.18: ‘The Tathagata does not exist after death’: this is an involvement with consciousness.
sn44.3:4.19: ‘The Tathagata both exists and does not exist after death’: this is an involvement with consciousness.
sn44.3:4.20: ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death’: this is an involvement with consciousness.
sn44.3:4.21: “This, friend, is the cause and reason why this has not been declared by the Blessed One.”
